metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic volume and behavior data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China. Used to calibrate SUMO simulation parameters and traffic demand patterns.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states in the Data Availability section that data is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Vehicle Extraction and Position Matrix Reform
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle centroids (xi, yi) from raw video and maps them to a binary position matrix of size X by Y, where a cell is assigned constant UV if a vehicle is present.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=3, tools unnamed, matrix dimensions specified but vehicle extraction method details are missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st.
nodes_process.description: Down-samples position matrices to reduce dimensions and stacks N consecutive steps into a temporal state tensor.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=3, stacking N=3 is defined but down-sampling ratio details are sparse.

nodes_process.source_quote: consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Constructs a dual-output DQN (multitask learning) predicting Q-values and auxiliary traffic metrics (speed/queue) simultaneously.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=4, architecture details fully specified in Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains the DQN using the Adam optimizer, target network freezing, and an epsilon-greedy strategy on a replay buffer.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=4, all critical hyperparameters and the algorithm (Algo 1) are explicitly detailed.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Tests the trained policy against baselines (no-control, PI-ALINEA) using 20 simulation experiments initialized with random seeds.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=4, evaluation environment and hardware are well specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into 8 subareas and iteratively removes data from each subarea to observe changes in travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: Clarity=4, the methodology for perturbation (Fig 15) is fully defined.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8 presents the Q-network training process... episode reward and mean travel time are both converged in 400,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curve showing the episode reward over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods and parameters specified; traffic data referenced but not provided via direct URL/DOI.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curve for mean travel time in seconds over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure largely specified but source data access is upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel time (min) comparison between No Control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL from 8:00 to 9:00.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Well-described scenarios and metrics; simulator SUMO is open-source.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times (s) for 20 experiments across No Control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL with percentage improvements.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed tabular results corresponding to stated methodology and 20 seed-initialized runs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed distribution by distance and time for (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: High-level visualization consistent with reported findings; source data access is a minor gap.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: On-ramp queue length (m) from 8:00 to 9:00 for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed queue length analysis based on SUMO simulation of described scenarios.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Correlation plots of occupancy (%) vs queue length (m) for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly presents calculated correlations from simulator outputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis box plots for travel time (s) across a baseline and 8 perturbed subareas.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method (subarea masking) clearly defined alongside resulting metrics.
